sentences.text: This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.494/2023 registered at Police Station Madhavnagar, District Ujjain (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 363, 366(A), 376(2)(N) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 5L/6 of the POCSO Act.
The applicant is in custody since 02/10/2023.

2. As per prosecution story, on 23/09/2023 the brother of the prosecutrix lodged an FIR at Police Station Madhavnagar by stating that his minor sister prosecutrix went to the School for examination, but she did not come back.
They tried to search her everywhere but could not find her.
During the investigation, it is found that applicant abducted the minor prosecutrix and took her with him and committed rape upon her.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 02/10/2023.
His earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew his prayer after examination of the prosecutrix.
Now prosecutrix has been examined before the trial Court and she has turned hostile and not supported the case of the prosecution.
Applicant is permanent resident of Ujjain district and is not having any criminal past.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.

Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.
4.

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident, therefore, applicant is not entitle for bail.

5. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.
6.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix has been examined before the trial Court and she has turned hostile; she categorically stated in her statement that present applicant has not committed any rape upon her and she voluntarily went with the applicant and solemnized marriage with him and final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
In these circumstances, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

7. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Tej Yash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167934733/
